subject: Demo recap + proposed network/interop test plan for hybrid inference
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@edgebank.com>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@edgebank.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo follow-up — hybrid/private deployment summary + next network tests

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks again for carving out time this morning — appreciate the candid discussion about your latency and compliance constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on today's demo:

- Summary of what we showed: hosted API for day-0 integration, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, and the Private (VPC/on-prem) control plane option with optional air-gap packaging. Highlight: automatic fallback routing to a verified open-model variant if primary model capacity is constrained.

- Key differentiators you asked about vs Hyperscaler X / managed endpoints:
  * Deterministic runtime knobs (per-route batching + KV cache) that let you tune tail latency without sacrificing unit cost.
  * Control plane separation: Private offers a customer-managed control plane (VPC peering or private link), giving you audit logs + KMS integration — Hyperscaler X requires cross-account IAM plumbing and doesn’t expose the same level of rollout hooks.
  * Air-gapped packaging is supported for on-prem deployments; the current limitation is one-way software bundle refresh cadence (we do staged offline upgrade). We'll validate upgrade window constraints in the PoC.

- Immediate asks from your side:
  1) Network path test: can your infra team run a traceroute and outbound-only connectivity check to our prep test endpoint? (we'll provide IPs).
  2) Control plane handshake: we need an approved list of CIDR ranges and the governance owner for cert exchange.
  3) SOC/Security: you flagged data residency and audit retention — attached is a stubbed SOC2 questions spreadsheet and a short test plan PDF.

Proposed timeline / next tests (subject to your availability):
- 05/23: infra-run network path + perf smoke (10-minute test, TCP + TLS handshake)
- 05/25–05/30: private PoC window (we'll set up a small dedicated pool in your VPC; 3 days of targeted load tests)

I attached a short "redwood_hybrid-test-plan.pdf" and a network topology image to this thread. Can Diego or Priya confirm who owns cert/key exchange and a preferred contact for scheduling the traceroute?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short technical call if helpful.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood_hybrid-test-plan.pdf (PDF), network_topology_stub.png (PNG), soc2-questions.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@edgebank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@edgebank.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgebank.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — hybrid/private deployment summary + next network tests

Thanks Soojin — great walkthrough. A few quick clarifications from our infra/security teams:

- Traceroute/IP test: yes, we can run the outbound tests on 05/23. Diego will run them from our pre-prod VPC and attach results. We prefer short-lived IPs/hostnames rather than long-lived endpoints for this.

- Control plane: our security owner is Priya (cc). For the cert exchange we need:
  * Details on the control-plane CA footprint
  * The exact CIDR set you will originate from (we prefer to whitelist via policy rather than broad ranges)

- Air-gap upgrades: curious what your offline bundle size is and whether the on-prem package requires a hardware appliance. Is the bundle signed and verifiable?

We also want to see a latency comparison for our 256-token test prompt between your Dedicated pool in our chosen region and Hyperscaler X managed endpoint (we can provide the prompt). Would you be able to run a 1000-request sample and share P50/P95/P99 across both? If that requires an extended PoC window we can accommodate.

Will run the traceroute on 05/23 and share. Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Morgan
Director of Platform Engineering | EdgeBank
alex.morgan@edgebank.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Demo follow-up — hybrid/private deployment summary + next network tests

Soojin — forwarding Alex's reply. Quick internal coordination notes / ask:

- Karthik: can you confirm exact CIDR ranges and whether we can provide ephemeral hostname IPs (short TTL) for the traceroute? We may need to spin up a small public-facing NAT in our infra to preserve minimal exposure.
- Marissa: pricing ask — Alex is explicitly asking for a 3-day Dedicated pool run and a head-to-head sample vs Hyperscaler X for 1k requests. Can you draft a constrained PoC commercial (credits + dedicated nodes) that covers 05/25–05/30? Keep it limited to the test objectives (latency/throughput, control-plane handshake).

Also: Karthik, Alex asked about bundle size/signing for air-gap. Can one of the platform engineers provide a 1-paragraph blurb we can share with the customer about how the on-prem bundles are signed and what the upgrade window/steps look like?

Tentative owner assignments:
- Network test prep (IPs, hostnames): Karthik / infra ops
- SOC/Security Qs: Soojin to coordinate with Priya on spreadsheet
- Commercial PoC: Marissa to send proposal by EOD 5/22

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@edgebank.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@edgebank.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgebank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — hybrid/private deployment summary + next network tests

Alex / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the asks. Confirming the plan and owners below:

1) Network path test (05/23) — Diego to run from pre-prod and share traceroute + TCP handshake times. Karthik will provide two ephemeral hostnames and a CIDR pair (one for control-plane egress, one for data-plane) by EOD 05/22. Hostnames will have a 2-hour TTL for the traceroute window.

2) Dedicated latency sample — Redwood will run a 1k request batch for your 256-token prompt against: (a) a Dedicated pool in us-west-2 configured to your desired instance size, and (b) Hyperscaler X managed endpoint (we'll proxy requests and capture timings). We'll deliver P50/P95/P99 and a short methods note. Target run: 05/26.

3) Air-gap / bundle questions — Karthik provided the blurb below (copied in):

"Redwood on-prem bundles are signed with our org-level signing key and timestamped. The distributor package is ~420MB compressed for the model runtime and control artifacts; updates are shipped as delta patches (typically <100MB). Customers may run the offline installer; the bundle includes a SHA256 manifest for verification. Upgrade windows are flexible but we recommend a maintenance window of 30–60 minutes for most single-node installs and 2–4 hours for clustered upgrades."

4) SOC/Security: I attached the SOC2 question sheet. Priya — could you flag any items you want the security docs to expand on? We'll assemble evidence and a short access matrix.

5) Commercial: Marissa will send a constrained PoC quote (credits + 3-day dedicated run) by EOD 05/22.

Next step: Diego, please reply with the traceroute result on 05/23 and paste it into the thread. If it helps, I'm happy to do a 20-minute call with your infra and security owners the morning of 05/24 to walk through the control-plane handshake steps.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the test results.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_hybrid-test-plan.pdf, soc2-questions.xlsx
